newsitem.title: USA: USDA'S GLICKMAN WANTS FOCUS ON AG CO-OPS,MARKETING.
newsitem.headline: USDA'S GLICKMAN WANTS FOCUS ON AG CO-OPS,MARKETING.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman asked his small-farm commission on Tuesday to give "fulsome consideration" to cooperatives as a way to help farmers through value-added production and marketing.

Glickman raised the issue on the same day President Clinton vetoed a tax break for sale of processing facilities to ag cooperatives. Clinton said the provision was poorly drafted and he would support enactment of a better version.
"We completely support the decision," said Glickman spokesman Tom Amontree.

In a letter to Harold Volkmer, chairman of the National Commission on Small Farms, Glickman said he wanted the commission to give consideration to "enhancing the ability of family-sized farm operations to form cooperatives for value-added production and marketing.

"While the department currently operates a number of programs for cooperatives, we need to redouble our efforts, evaluate the programs, strengthen the ones that work and implement new initiatives as necessary," Glickman wrote.
